corpus_provenance: NEWLY AUTHORED. The 68-phase source plan (phases.json), the coded bodies and the two-decode-target / five-template DD structure shape are transcribed from the numbers already pinned in the Rust consumer crates/rtc-media/src/regression/dd_one_rid_literal.rs:40-199 and dd_one_rid_counterexample.rs:143-233,493-510,620-747. No expected output value is authored: every emitted field is measured from real Go execution over a real pion vnet + DTLS/SRTP DownTrack capture.
scope: Proves, for the authored 68-phase plan, the original public buffer.Buffer.Write -> ReadExtended -> DownTrack.WriteRTP admission decision, the original Simulcast + DD temporal selector + DDTemporal munger + DDForwarder output (frame-number rebase, active decode target mask, structure attachment), the dropped-slot padding packet, and the far-side SRTP sequence numbers / timestamps / markers / payload bytes, for VP9 and AV1 in both ONE_SPATIAL_LAYER_PER_STREAM modes. The RID layer switch goes through the real target-only allocation path (SetMaxTemporalLayer + SetMaxSpatialLayer + ProvisionalAllocatePrepare/Allocate/Commit) and the cross-RID clock through the real DownTrack.HandleRTCPSenderReportData. Does NOT prove: live server signalling or SDK interop; real decoder pixel output; congestion control or pacer timing (PassThrough pacer + null BWE, authored wall-clock pacing); RTX/NACK repair; the stream allocator's own bandwidth estimation (the published bitrate table is an authored input); real RTCP wire transport of the sender reports (they are injected at the public DownTrack entry point, not received as SRTCP); any DD structure other than the single authored two-decode-target / five-template one; or the Rust engine's own timing histogram.
